answer_1.quote: In this paper, we present PNEG, a Promptbased NEgative response Generation method leveraging a large-scale language model... Our method can generate high-quality adversarial negative responses only with a few human-written examples.

answer_2.quote: We evaluate the quality of adversarial responses with predictive scores of the response selection model and context-response similarity model... We report the R@1 and mean reciprocal rank (MRR) score.

answer_4.quote: For human evaluation, we randomly sampled 100 data... Each response is evaluated by three human annotators. We recruited a total of 9 human annotators...
answer_4.guideline: Human annotators classify the type of each negative response as random, hard, and false negative according to the review criteria described in the DailyDialog++.
